newsitem.title: UK: Aluminium demand may be understated - Macquarie.
newsitem.headline: Aluminium demand may be understated - Macquarie.

text.p: Underlying aluminium demand this year may be understated, due to the effects of stocking and de-stocking, Macquarie Equities Ltd said.

"The implications are that reported demand overstated underlying consumption in 1994 and 1995, but is severely underestimating underlying consumption in 1996 - possibly by as much as 350,000/400,000 tonnes," Macquarie said in its latest weekly review.
Analysing comparative consumption trends in copper and aluminium Macquarie said the build-up in semi-fabricated stocks added 400,000 tonnes to 1994 aluminium demand.

Another 150,000 tonnes was added to demand in 1995, broken down by a 250,000 tonnes build in the first half of the year, followed by a 100,000-tonne drawdown in semis stocks in the latter half of the year.
"De-stocking of semis has continued in 1996 and is estimated to have reduced demand by around 380,000 tonnes," it said.

Stocking cycles suggest that even modest growth in underlying consumption could yield a strong recovery in demand in 1997. Macquarie forecast 4.3-percent growth in reported consumption, although this may turn out to be an underestimate.
